headline: Remnant showers and flood concerns fade today, followed by dry and much warmer weather Monday and Tuesday
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Bands of showers rotating around the remnants of Isaias continue across Central Kentucky this morning, with low clouds, patchy fog and locally heavier downpours. Rain coverage decreases from west to east this afternoon and evening. Clearing may allow patchy fog overnight, then high pressure and southwest flow bring sunny, dry and much warmer weather Monday and Tuesday.

days.label: Sunday
days.precipitation: 45–60% through early afternoon; decreasing to 20–35% late afternoon and evening; 10% or less overnight
days.hazard: No official NWS watch or warning at issuance; isolated heavier showers may cause brief ponding, and patchy fog may develop tonight where skies clear
days.forecast: Cloudy and cool with scattered to numerous showers through early afternoon. A few bands may briefly produce heavier rain or a rumble of thunder, but severe weather is not expected. Showers taper and clouds gradually lift from west to east late today and this evening. Partial clearing overnight may support patchy fog.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No significant weather hazards expected after any early patchy fog dissipates
days.forecast: Any early fog or low cloud clears quickly. Mostly sunny, dry and much warmer conditions follow as ridging and southwest flow strengthen. Winds remain light, and the afternoon warms into the lower to middle 80s.

days.label: Tuesday
days.forecast: Sunny to mostly sunny, dry and unseasonably warm. Southwest winds around 5–10 mph accompany afternoon temperatures in the middle to upper 80s. Mostly clear and mild conditions continue Tuesday night.

kentucky.bottomLine: Showers and low clouds linger today, then end from west to east. After possible patchy fog tonight, Monday and Tuesday turn sunny, dry and sharply warmer, with no significant weather hazards expected.
kentucky.confidence: High on the dry and warm Monday–Tuesday pattern; moderate-high on today's west-to-east drying; moderate on localized shower totals and tonight's fog coverage

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson / Central primary · Tempest excluded
upstate.summary: The cold front trailing the remnants of Isaias is moving through the Upstate this morning. Any remaining showers or isolated thunder should exit east by midday, but an official Flood Watch remains in effect through 2 PM because saturated ground and runoff can prolong flooding. Clouds break this afternoon, followed by dry, sunny and much warmer weather Monday and Tuesday.

currentConditions.condition: Network observations are WeatherFlow–Tempest-fed and excluded; official KCEU and KLQK observations used instead

days.label: Sunday
days.precipitation: 20–35% through late morning; 10% or less after 2 PM and tonight
days.hazard: Official NWS Flood Watch through 2 PM; residual flash flooding, high water and mountain landslides remain possible, while an isolated strong wind gust or brief tornado is conditionally possible before the front clears
days.forecast: Mostly cloudy this morning with a few remaining showers and possibly an isolated thunderstorm. The front shifts east by midday, ending the widespread rain threat. Clouds then break during the afternoon while southwest winds remain occasionally gusty. Mostly clear and drier conditions arrive tonight.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No significant weather hazards expected near Clemson and Central; northwest gusts of 25–35 mph remain possible along the higher Blue Ridge elevations
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and considerably warmer. Light west winds are expected near Clemson and Central, while higher mountain ridges remain breezy. Clear conditions Monday night support a wide local temperature spread.

days.label: Tuesday
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and unseasonably warm beneath strengthening upper-level ridging. Winds remain light, with afternoon temperatures in the middle to upper 80s. Clear and mild weather continues Tuesday night.

upstate.bottomLine: The heavy-rain episode is ending, but the Flood Watch remains important through 2 PM because runoff and high water can persist. Conditions improve rapidly this afternoon, followed by sunny, dry and much warmer weather Monday and Tuesday.
upstate.confidence: High on afternoon improvement and the dry Monday–Tuesday pattern; moderate-high on today's temperature; moderate on the final shower timing and residual flooding extent

sourceNotes: Official airport observations span 8:15–8:20 AM EDT. KDVK had a 400-foot overcast ceiling, KLEX reported fog/mist with northwest wind, and both Upstate airports were mostly cloudy with southwest wind. No Tempest observations were used.

The NWS point forecasts were generated at 8:45 AM EDT. Danville has a 50% shower chance today, a high near 65°F and a low near 54°F before warming to 82°F Monday and 85°F Tuesday. Clemson has a high near 71°F today, then 84°F Monday and Tuesday with essentially no rain after this morning.

Official hazards are distinct from the independent forecast: no active alert covered Danville at issuance, while the Greenville–Spartanburg Flood Watch remained in effect for Clemson, Central and surrounding Upstate areas through 2 PM because additional heavy showers and runoff could prolong flooding.

The Louisville discussion expects remnant shower bands to pivot across Central Kentucky this morning, with most areas receiving another 0.25–0.50 inch and isolated higher totals, followed by gradual west-to-east clearing. The Greenville–Spartanburg discussion expects the trailing front to sweep east this morning, ending widespread rain while leaving a conditional isolated severe threat before frontal passage.

Model inventories checked at 8:46 AM EDT showed complete 06Z HRRR through hour 48, 09Z RAP through hour 51, 06Z NAM through hour 84, 06Z NAM 3-km Nest through hour 60, 06Z GFS and GEFS through hour 384 and complete 00Z ECMWF through hour 360. The 06Z ECMWF was still running but already available through hour 144.

College of DuPage radar at 8:40 AM EDT showed the main convective rain shield east of the Carolinas, with disorganized remnant showers rotating across Kentucky and nearby portions of the Tennessee and Ohio Valleys. Clean-infrared imagery at 8:41 AM showed the deepest convection displaced east of the forecast regions while lower remnant cloud cover persisted inland.

HRRR, RAP and NAM agree on a cool Sunday across Central Kentucky and post-frontal warming in the Upstate. GFS and ECMWF agree on widespread 80s Monday, and their broader ridge pattern supports continued warmth Tuesday. Ranges remain broad enough to cover clearing-timing and local-elevation differences.

Clemson Weather Network identifies its observations as WeatherFlow–Tempest data. Those observations were excluded, and official KCEU and KLQK observations were used for Upstate analysis and verification.

The forecast-accuracy summary generated at 2:35 PM EDT October 10 was consulted. KDVK overnight ranges were shifted downward using the recommended -2°F low correction. Upstate overnight ranges were widened because KCEU retains a recommended +1.5°F low correction while KLQK retains a recommended -2.5°F correction. No daytime station correction was applied.

HRRR remains the best overall high-temperature model with a 1.6°F mean absolute error. RAP follows at 2.6°F, while ECMWF, NAM and GFS have larger overall errors. Forecast ranges were kept near 5–7°F wide because overall range coverage is 59.3%, 72-hour coverage is 54.2% and the limited post-tropical transition samples remain less reliable than the post-frontal high-pressure category. The 5%-or-less dry probabilities are consistent with the low observed frequency in the 0–20% reliability bin. This candidate does not modify the repository, forecast archive, website or widget.

appliedAdjustments.details: Shifted the lower portion of overnight ranges downward using KDVK's updated recommended -2°F low correction; KLEX remains below the correction threshold. No high-temperature station correction was applied. Tuesday's range was widened because 72-hour range coverage is only 54.2%.

Widened overnight ranges in both directions because KCEU has a recommended +1.5°F low correction while KLQK has a recommended -2.5°F correction. HRRR received the greatest overall model weight, with official observations and the NWS point forecast anchoring today's post-frontal temperature.
